job: Release the current cruush 1.5 fixes: preserve the fixed global bug-report control, keep desktop map profile panels at a usable phone width, shift the bottom navigation away from open panels, force the full-page mobile profile treatment when width or height cannot fit the desktop composition, and run the exact worktree locally with seeded profiles plus one active Ping. Private-message images may contain nonhuman subjects or multiple adults, while gore, hate symbols, violence, screenshots, image text or URLs, and people who appear underage remain blocked. Profile photos remain limited to one adult human. Remove redundant private-message toolbar labels and icons without changing timer behavior. Make map heart units 15 percent larger than their current enlarged size on hover, keyboard focus, and long-press preview while preserving their default size. Include the existing approved profile, appeal, moderation, activity, distance, and carousel fixes in this release.
preserved: Keep private trans status as the eligibility gate for the optional T4T crowd; do not infer it from a selected gender identity.
Keep birth-control choices encrypted with other sensitive profile health data.
Keep profile overlays open after cruush and message actions unless the user explicitly closes or leaves them.
Keep the signed-in support flow and general public support flow unchanged.
Keep the existing appeal evidence requirements, encryption, 24-hour expiry, moderation visibility, and reports inbox delivery unchanged.
Keep rejected non-age photos deleted and never expose suspended-photo evidence outside authenticated moderator routes.
Keep profile-photo adult-human and single-person checks separate from private-message image policy.
Keep the default map heart size, map interactions, badges, profile opening, SF and VC layers, and marker stacking unchanged.
Preserve all unrelated worktrees and user changes.
nonGoals: Do not change T4T eligibility, crowd visibility, identity-change locks, or health privacy rules.
Do not add a database column for birth control or expose it in moderation text.
Do not delete an account, block a sender, or remove unrelated mutuals when dismissing an incoming cruush.
Do not redesign the appeal form or change authentication, suspension policy, moderation decisions, email providers, or environment configuration.
Do not redesign bottom-navigation icons or change the global mobile breakpoint used by unrelated routes.
Do not claim that a web app can prevent operating-system or browser screenshots.
Do not attach sensitive images to email or create a public media URL.
Do not weaken CSAM, underage, gore, hate-symbol, violence, screenshot, image-text, or image-URL enforcement in private messages.
Do not modify or discard the existing local carousel, Settings, or bug-button work.
Do not commit, push, or deploy without a separate user request.
